Testimony of Senator Donna Bailey introducing
LD 37, Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in Old Orchard Beach the Captain Christopher S.
Cash Memorial Bridge Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
Thursday, February 27, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and Esteemed Members of the Joint Standing Committee
on Transportation, my name is Donna Bailey, and I proudly represent Senate District 31, which includes Buxton, Old Orchard Beach, and Saco. Today I am pleased to introduce my bill LD 37,
"Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in Old Orchard Beach the Captain Christopher S. Cash Memorial Bridge." It directs the Department of Transportation to rename Goosefare Brook Bridge after a local hero who died in service to his country.
Captain Christopher S. Cash, Sr. was a man who committed his life to helping others. Chris was known for his passions of rumiing and fitness, his love for his family, and his dedication to our
country. After graduating from Old Orchard Beach High School, Chris enlisted in the United
States Army in 1986, eventually earning the rank of Captain. He enjoyed a career that
incorporated his love for country, helping others, and being physically active.
In October 2003, he was mobilized in support of Operation Iraqi Freedom as the Commander of Company A, 1st Battalion, 120th Infantry Regiment, 30th Enhanced Separate Infantry Brigade, which was headquartered in Jacksonville, North Carolina. As a Company Commander, he led
three platoons, and his soldiers provided support and protection to Iraqi citizens.
On June 24, 2004, Captain Cash personally led one of his platoons on a mission to secure two
critical bridges in the center of Baqubah, Iraq. While traveling, the platoon was engaged by insurgents. Captain Cash was mortally wounded by a machine gunner while focusing on the
safety of his men and ordering them to take cover. At that moment, Captain Cash paid the ultimate price to protect his soldiers, a job which he took very seriously. He touched the lives of
all that he met, and they will forever be blessed by knowing him.
By renaming the bridge in memory of Captain Christopher S. Cash, we can help his family honor
his legacy and his service to our country. Chris dedicated his life to helping, caring for, and inspiring others -- his family, friends, community, and country. Hopefully, by renaming the
bridge we can preserve Captain Cash's memory and legacy for everyone.

I thank the Committee for its time, and I would be happy to answer any questions

Testimony of Rep. Lori K. Gramlich in support of

.

LD 37, Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in Old Orchard Beach the Captain

Christopher S. Cash Memorial Bridge

Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and esteemed colleagues of the Transportation Committee, my
name is Lori K. Gramlich, and I represent the lovely seaside community of Old Orchard Beach, House
District 131. I am honored to submit this testimony as a cosponsor in support of LD 37, Resolve, to
Rename a Bridge in Old Orchard Beach the Captain Christopher S. Cash Memorial Bridge.

This Resolve proposes renaming Bridge 3643 on Seaside Avenue, which crosses Goose Fare Creek in the Ocean Park community of Old Orchard Beach, to the Captain Christopher S. Cash Memorial Bridge. This bridge is currently known as the Goose Fare Bridge. This designation would serve as a lasting tribute to a
man who gave his life in service to our country, embodying the highest ideals of courage, sacrifice and
dedication.

Captain Cash was more than just a soldier; he was a leader, a mentor and a cherished member of his community. His unwavering commitment to duty and his willingness to make the ultimate sacrifice in defense of our freedoms deserve to be permanently recognized. Naming the bridge in his honor would not only commemorate his legacy but also serve as a powerful reminder to all who pass through of the values
he stood for--duty, honor and service.

I had the good fortune of knowing Chris's mom, Nancy Lee Kelley, who passed away in November of 2022. Nancy was a tireless advocate for her son, his memory and legacy, and for all the Gold Star families
who have had to endure the unspeakable tragedy of losing a child.

Bridges symbolize connection and resilience, much like Chris Cash did throughout his life. By dedicating the Goose Fare Bridge in his name, we ensure that his memory endures and that future generations
understand and appreciate his legacy. Doing so would be a lasting tribute with profound meaning to his
family and our community - all of whom continue to mourn his loss.

Additional costs to the Department of Transportation associated with signage are expected to be minor and can be absorbed within budgeted resources.

I respectfully urge you to approve this proposal in recognition of Captain Christopher Cash's bravery and service. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Testimony of Meghan Russo Maine Department of Transportation
Before the 132"" Legislature, Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
Neither For Nor Against
LD 37, Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in Old Orchard Beach the Captain Christopher S.
Cash Memorial Bridge

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation, I am Meghan Russo, Director of Government Affairs at MaineDOT. MaineDOT is neither for nor against LD 37 and normally does not testify on bills
that propose to name roads and bridges, but because this is the first such bill in this Legislature, we hope that an overview of past practice regarding such bills will be helpful.
MaineDOT considers the naming of bridges, roadways, and other state transportation infrastructure to be within the purview of the Legislature. Simply put, we build them and you name them. Accordingly, we generally do not take positions on so-called "naming bills." However, we usually submit written testimony regarding whether the particular infrastructure under consideration has been named before, and if so what those name(s) are. In this case, we
are not aware of any previous legislatively-sanctioned names for this structure.
We also note that the Committee historically has asked sponsors of naming bills to produce
written evidence of support for the proposed name from the municipality or municipalities in which the infrastructure is located. This avoids some local issues that have prompted renaming
bills in the past.
We hope this information is helpful. In the future, we will simply submit written testimony on
bills that seek to name transportation infrastructure. Thank you for your time. I am happy to answer any questions you may have.
